newsitem.title: USA: Amerihost agreement ended, Q1 charge seen.
newsitem.headline: Amerihost agreement ended, Q1 charge seen.

text.p: Amerihost Properties Inc said it expects to incur a non-recurring first-quarter charge of about $1.7 million related to the termination of a business development and consulting agreement between the company and Urban 2000 Corp.

It said Richard D'Onofrio has resigned as executive vice president and director of Amerihost to pursue other interests. The company and Urban 2000, which is owned by Amerihost chairman H. Andrew Torchia and D'ONofrio, mutually agreed to terminate Urban's development and consultant agreement.

In connection with these changes, Amerihost said the compensation packages for Michael Holtz, its president and chief executive officer, and Russell Cerqua, its chief financial officer, were significantly reduced with all future bonuses determined by the board of directors based on the company's performance.
Going forward, Amerihost said its expenses will be reduced by approximately $500,000 in 1997 and $800,000 a year after that.

Amerihost, a hotel development and management company, also said it plans to increase the number of outside directors on its six-member board. Holtz said the board currently is down one member, and a replacement will come from outside the company, bringing a 50-50 split to outside-inside representation.
By next year, Holtz said he expects outside directors will constitute four directors and inside directors, two.
"As the company continues to expand its presence in the hotel industry, it will be able to attract additional talented directors to its board," said Torchia in a statement.

President Holtz, in a statement, noted, "The company recently opened its 42nd AmeriHost Inn hotel in Anderson, Calif., and currently has another 18 hotels under construction. For 1996, the same room sales for the AmeriHost Inn brand were up 14.5 percent.

"These strong operational results coupled with the changes made should assist the company in improving the company's EBITDA and net income as it continues to grow the AmeriHost Inn chain in small towns," Holtz continued.
